title: DuckDuckGo is telling schools they can turn its AI off, and keep search
friendlyTitle: DuckDuckGo is telling schools they can turn its AI off and still have search
summary: TechCrunch reports that DuckDuckGo is pitching schools after Google's decision to leave Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search off for student accounts until an administrator turns them on, with Search tied to AI features. Founder Gabriel Weinberg pointed schools to DuckDuckGo's deploy documentation and said to get in touch. The company told TechCrunch that Google could turn Search's AI features off for schools if it wanted to. DuckDuckGo is not an AI-free company: it has Duck.ai and an AI search assistant. Unlike the Google setup in dispute, it says those features can be switched off in search and in the browser, and it runs a separate site, noai.duckduckgo.com, where AI-assisted answers, AI images, and AI feature suggestions are off.
friendlySummary: TechCrunch reports that DuckDuckGo is offering itself to schools after Google said Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will stay off for student accounts until an administrator turns them on, with Search tied to AI features. Founder Gabriel Weinberg pointed schools to DuckDuckGo's install guide and said to get in touch. The company told TechCrunch that Google could turn Search's AI features off for schools if it wanted to. DuckDuckGo is not an AI-free company. It has its own chat tool, Duck.ai, and an AI search assistant. It says those features can be switched off in search and in the browser. It also runs a separate site, noai.duckduckgo.com, where AI answers, AI images, and AI suggestions are off.
whyItMatters: Yesterday's switch was Google's. Today's practical option, if a school wants search without an AI answer on top, is a different default, not a setting inside Google that Google has not offered. noai.duckduckgo.com is a URL you can open and check. It does not replace Classroom, and it does not remove AI from every other tab a student can open.
